question: Does retained update history expose non-immediate exact relationships that beat periodic journal+checkpoint storage under the same bounded reconstruction depth?

oracle.neutral_compressor: zlib-9 applied identically to serialized snapshot/delta records

result.linear_histories: append/front-insert/middle-edit selected the immediate predecessor; generic parent choice was ~1.0008x journal bytes, so history alone provides no new gain.
result.alternating_branch_history: fixed-checkpoint non-immediate parent selection reached ~0.220x journal total bytes and ~0.317x mean selective-read bytes at the same depth<=7 bound.
result.independent_control: generic parent search did not beat journal bytes and must be rejected by complete-byte admission.
result.greedy_global_policy_negative: a separate greedy checkpoint/parent policy regressed a middle-edit hostile by ~2.28x versus periodic journal, so greedy temporal parenting is retired.

interpretation: The surviving signal is non-immediate version-family structure among retained states, not a universal 'temporal' representation. Existing EntropyGraph/Mosaic-style relation machinery is the strongest simpler control; A08 is not chartered as a new format thesis.
next_discriminator: Use a preregistered retained-generation trace with branching/reversion/nonlocal recurrence and compare current journal/checkpoint semantics against existing version-family graph ownership. Require complete stored bytes, update wall, selective generation recovery, failure-domain cost and zero carrying cost for current-state-only archives.

external_control.observation: Git already compares nearby objects within a bounded --window for delta compression and caps delta-chain --depth because deeper chains increase unpack cost. Pack entries may delta from another base object using copy/insert instructions.
external_control.implication: Non-immediate bounded delta-parent selection is mature prior art, not an A08 novelty claim. Any CMPCT A08 contribution must come from transactional retained-history semantics, content-only opportunity discovery, recovery/failure-domain co-design, or a stronger exact ownership model.
